requirements.title: Associating entities have selector rank and bounds with no ALLOCATABLE or POINTER attributes
requirements.definition: Within ASSOCIATE, CHANGE TEAM, or SELECT TYPE, each associating entity has the same rank as its selector. Each lower bound is the LBOUND result for the corresponding selector dimension, and each upper bound is lower bound plus extent minus one. The associating entity does not have ALLOCATABLE or POINTER.

pending.no-allocatable-attribute-source: PENDING source-control contrast showing ALLOCATE/deallocate or allocatable-only contexts cannot be applied to the associate name solely because the selector is allocatable; any diagnostic is filed under ALLOCATE or attribute-owner rules.
pending.no-pointer-attribute-source: PENDING source-control contrast showing pointer assignment to the associate name is not admitted merely because the selector is a pointer, except where 11.1.3.3 p5/C1101 permits pointer association context through a definable selector.

requirements.oracle:
LBOUND/UBOUND/SHAPE inquiries are acceptable only because this paragraph requires the expected bounds; future plans must avoid circular use of array-section formation as the sole oracle.

S11.1.3.3-001 ASSOCIATE rank and bounds runtime fixtures: three complete run/effect/f2023 programs observe rank and bounds with inquiry functions whose expected results are required by p1. The rank case associates tile with a rank-two section grid(-1:3:2,8:12:4), assigns SHAPE(tile) to a length-two integer vector, and requires [3,2]. The lower-bound case checks both a whole-array selector, for which LBOUND(whole,1) is the nondefault declared lower bound -5, and a section selector base(-3:3:2), for which LBOUND(sec,1) is 1 even though the selected subscripts run from -3 to 3. The upper-bound case associates vec with base(12:20:3), whose extent is 3 and whose LBOUND result is 1, so UBOUND(vec,1) must be 1+3-1 = 3 rather than the selector subscript upper bound 20 or underlying array upper bound 21.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future ASSOCIATE fixtures must use non-vacuous selectors and sentinels: lower bounds must differ where bounds are asserted, character length must be checked with LEN rather than inferred from padded comparison, outer homonyms must start with values different from any inner assignment, and assignment through an associate name is credited only after the selector is established definable. No plan may count selector evaluations, depend on function side effects, assume a real or complex kind exists, or use compiler agreement as an oracle.

S11.1.3.3-001 ASSOCIATE rank and bounds fixture boundaries: only same-rank-as-selector, nondefault-lower-bound and upper-bound-from-extent are represented. The section-bound fixtures deliberately make associating-entity bounds differ from selector subscript bounds and underlying declared bounds, so copying those bounds would fail. The whole-array lower-bound control catches a processor that defaulted every associate-name lower bound to 1. no-allocatable-attribute-source and no-pointer-attribute-source remain pending as source/diagnostic contrasts rather than runtime effects.

requirements.title: Associating entities have selector corank and selector cobounds for coarray selectors
requirements.definition: Within ASSOCIATE, SELECT RANK, or SELECT TYPE, each associating entity has the same corank as its selector. If the selector is a coarray, the cobounds of each codimension of the associating entity are the same as those of the selector.

requirements.title: Associating entities inherit ASYNCHRONOUS, VOLATILE, dynamic type, optional absence, and contiguity properties as specified
requirements.definition: Within ASSOCIATE, CHANGE TEAM, SELECT RANK, or SELECT TYPE, the associating entity has ASYNCHRONOUS or VOLATILE if and only if the selector is a variable and has the attribute. If polymorphic, it assumes the selector dynamic type and type parameter values. It does not have OPTIONAL; an OPTIONAL selector cannot be absent. It is contiguous if and only if the selector is contiguous.

requirements.title: Associating entities are variables but are not definable when their selectors are not definable or not permitted in definition contexts
requirements.definition: The associating entity itself is a variable. If the selector is not a definable variable, the associating entity is not definable and shall not be defined or become undefined. If a selector is not permitted in a variable definition context, neither the associate name nor any subobject of it shall appear in a variable definition context or pointer association context.

pending.nondefinable-selector-definition-rejecte: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the selector is a nondefinable variable (for example protected or otherwise prohibited by its owner) and the associate name is assigned; the repair changes only to a definable selector.
pending.nondefinable-selector-undefinition-rejec: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the associate name for a nondefinable selector would become undefined, repaired by using a definable selector or removing the undefinition context.
pending.selector-not-vdc-associate-definition-re: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the selector is not permitted in a variable definition context and only the associate name appears in such a context; the repair changes that one context or selector.
pending.selector-not-vdc-pointer-association-rej: PENDING diagnostic/control pair where the associate name or subobject appears in a pointer association context although the selector is not permitted in a variable definition context; the repair uses a selector permitted in that context.

S11.1.3.3-005 ASSOCIATE definability runtime fixture: one complete run/positive-control/f2023 program observes definability through a definable variable selector. The selector is the triplet section store(6:8), which has no vector subscript and is initialized to values distinct from the assigned values. Inside ASSOCIATE, vec is assigned [601,602,603]; after END ASSOCIATE the corresponding selector elements store(6:8) must hold those values while neighboring store(5) remains 50. A copy-only, expression-only or nondefinable associate-name rule would not update the selector.
